st.headline: China’s trade surplus soars past US$1 trillion as AI boom powers exports
st.teaser: China’s trade surplus tops US$1 trillion for a second consecutive year, reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.
fullText: BEIJING – China’s trade surplus surged past US$1 trillion (S$1.3 trillion) in the first 10 months as a global race to build artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure buoyed sales of high-tech products and helped offset weak domestic demand, a dynamic likely to sharpen tensions with major trading partners.
The figures highlight Beijing’s growing reliance on overseas demand to support an economy hobbled by subdued consumption and a protracted property slump.

But while the global AI investment boom is expected to keep demand for Chinese technology products strong into 2027, it risks deepening domestic imbalances and fuelling trade frictions with partners including the European Union (EU).

Exports rose sharply by 35.2% in October from the same month in 2025 in US dollar terms, customs data showed on Nov 10, only a touch slower than the 36.3% surge in September, but ahead of economists’ forecast for an increase of 33.5%.
That helped lift China’s trade surplus to US$1.04 trillion in the first 10 months, topping US$1 trillion for a second consecutive year and reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.

The swelling surplus could fuel further tensions with the EU, where leaders have called for more trade curbs with China after reaching an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the bloc over the next few years.
Because the measures have yet to take effect, factories are expected to bring forward shipments, bolstering exports in the near term.

China on Nov 9 officially announced the extension of a trade truce with Washington due to expire on Nov 10 by two months, but said last week that expanding its purchases of American farm goods would hinge on the implementation of their agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement.

“The risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers continue expanding their presence in overseas markets,” said Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China.
Imports grew 41.6%, beating the median forecast for a 32% increase in the Reuters poll and accelerating from the 31% growth in September.

China’s trade surplus with the US dipped slightly to US$32.71 billion in October from US$34.01 billion the previous month, but the larger gap remains a point of friction between the two economic superpowers.
Oil imports fell 13.3% from a year earlier, though shipments reached their highest level since March as buyers sought supplies after the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted Middle East flows.

The trade data comes ahead of next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, where Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump are expected to meet for the third time in 2026, putting trade frictions and tariff policy squarely in focus .
Following a September summit between Xi and Trump in Washington, the two sides proposed a US$60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts, including roughly US$17 billion worth of US farm goods.
One big worry for Beijing is that consumers remain reluctant to spend, constrained by a property market downturn that has battered household wealth and dented confidence in the economic outlook.

Sluggish demand at home has pushed Chinese carmakers to seek sales in overseas markets. China’s car exports maintained a solid pace of growth in October, while domestic vehicle sales recorded a 12th straight month of declines, separate data released by an industry association showed.
Greater reliance on exports, however, leaves China’s economy increasingly exposed to any slowdown in global demand.
Much of the strength in exports in 2026 has been fuelled by a global push to expand AI infrastructure.

“The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last,” Macquarie analysts wrote. They expect China’s exports to accelerate further in the fourth quarter before starting to slow from the first quarter of 2027. REUTERS

cna.headline: Chipmaker Infineon forecasts strong 2027 growth on data-centre demand
cna.teaser: Chipmaker Infineon forecasts strong 2027 growth on data-centre demand
fullText: BERLIN, Nov 10 : Infineon on Tuesday forecast 2027 revenue growth of more than 20 per cent and an increase of about 5 per centage points in profitability, driven by demand from data centres, power infrastructure and software-defined vehicles.

• The German chipmaker reported fourth-quarter revenue of €4.706 billion ($5.28 billion) and a segment result of €1.119 billion, yielding a segment margin of 23.8 per cent. For the full fiscal year, revenue rose 12 per cent to €16.353 billion, while adjusted free cash flow reached €1.925 billion
• CEO Jochen Hanebeck said the company was entering the new fiscal year with "continued strong momentum", supported by an ongoing cyclical recovery and demand in structural growth markets
• For 2027, Infineon forecasts revenue of around €20 billion, including close to €4 billion from data-centre power supplies
• The company also plans to propose raising its dividend to €0.38 per share from €0.35
